text:
Pseudoics
They'd need to go to 10nm next year, if they just drop to 12nm then I doubt that a 30% increase can be achieved. They may find improvements so that DX12 will show a nice bump, but it wont reflect in DX11. The TDP is at 250W for the 1080ti, which is the same as the 980ti on 28nm. I doubt that you'll get 30% on architecture alone, it would need that die shrink.

Unless of course they go the route of FuryX and water cool, Fury is 275W TDP with a 120mm fan, so if they look at a 240mm solution they might up the stakes to 300W TDP.

My guess is that Volta based 2080 cards if they are on 12nm as rumoured, which is only a half shrink from 16nm, which is much less percentage wise (50% node) than the shrink from 28 to 16 which is 85% node. May have 20% on DX 11 over 1080 cards(180W TDP), but not matching the 1080 ti except possibly in DX12. Which would leave them 30% possibly on a 2080 ti over a 1080 ti, but only in DX12.

But that's dependant on going to 12nm, if they don't then their next ti card will probably be water cooled.
author: @magottyk

text:
We shall see mate. There's already 10%+ in cuda cores left on the table with the Titan XP/1080ti being cut down from the full GP102 found in the Quadro 6000, which is only a 471mm2 chip. So long as they don't release a Titan XP Black or whatever (unlikely), only a 20% improvement is needed over Pascal to reach your goal and have the GTX2080 look good. 

Maxwell was also a new uarch on the same node and that brought significant gains. Assuming something similar - and yes, specifically in DX12 - whilst releasing Volta 2080 at similar die sizes to GP102, and building the release out to monolithic flagship sizes over 600mm2,  there's room for a new (successful) uarch to reach 40%+ over Pascal with Titan X Volta, even on 16nm. Any process shrinks that may be true will make that even easier. Power wise, HBM2 will free up the thermal envelope and I wouldn't expect more than 250w for various reasons, even if it uses much more with a good OC as they do.

Having a strong DX12 uarch from both camps should finally see devs target the benefits of it. Multi-core/multi-thread/multi-engine is the future until some revolutionary processor comes along. I'm more interested in seeing what AMD pulls off with Navi.
